summary: The reader has done an undergraduate computer science degree: discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, primes and gcd, sets, induction, recurrences and asymptotics), basic linear algebra over the reals and complex numbers (matrices, inverses, norms), polynomials and complex roots of unity, and algorithms including divide and conquer and Karatsuba multiplication. On the machine side they know basic single- and multi-tape Turing machines and the idea of counting steps. They have not studied the Fourier transform, FFT-based multiplication, Schonhage-Strassen, Harvey-van der Hoeven, numerical error analysis, abstract algebra beyond rings of residues, finite-field linear algebra, or any lower-bound or advanced tape-algorithm technique, so those must be explained.

known.name: Modular arithmetic and residue rings
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers taken modulo q, where addition and multiplication wrap around and numbers coprime to q have inverses.

known.name: Primes, coprimality and the Euclidean algorithm
known.gloss: Primes, the gcd of two integers, coprime integers, and the Euclidean algorithm that computes gcds and Bezout coefficients (hence modular inverses).

known.name: Positional (radix) number representation
known.gloss: Writing a nonnegative integer as a sum of digits times powers of a base, with binary the case b = 2, so a number is a list of digits.

known.name: Signed binary numbers and rounding
known.gloss: Representing negative integers in binary and the floor, ceiling and round-to-nearest operations on real numbers.

known.name: Dyadic rationals
known.gloss: Rational numbers of the form m/2^k, which have finite binary expansions and can be stored exactly with a fixed number of bits.

known.name: Bitwise operations and Hamming weight
known.gloss: Bit-level operations such as XOR on binary strings, and the Hamming weight, the number of ones in a bit string.

known.name: Permutations and bijections
known.gloss: A one-to-one rearrangement of a finite set of positions, with its inverse and composition.

known.name: Lexicographic order and multi-index addressing
known.gloss: Ordering tuples by comparing first coordinates first, so a multidimensional array can be stored in a flat sequence with each position given by a tuple of indices.

known.name: Matrix algebra
known.gloss: Products, inverses, transposes and diagonal matrices as linear maps on vectors, including complex matrices.

known.name: Vector norms and the triangle inequality
known.gloss: Measuring the size of a vector (for example by its largest coordinate) and bounding the size of sums and linear images.

known.name: Logarithms, exponentials and floor/ceiling in analysis
known.gloss: Basic properties of logarithms and exponentials, powers with real exponents, and comparison of growth rates such as n(lg n)^(1-kappa) versus n lg n.

known.name: Theta, Omega and little-o notation
known.gloss: Asymptotic notation beyond O: tight bounds, lower bounds and bounds where the ratio tends to zero.

known.name: Summations and geometric series
known.gloss: Closed forms for sums of powers, geometric series, and telescoping sums.

known.name: Recurrence relations and divide and conquer
known.gloss: Cost recurrences such as T(n) = a T(n/b) + f(n), solved by unrolling levels of recursion and summing the costs.

known.name: Schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication
known.gloss: The O(n^2) digit-by-digit multiplication algorithm and Karatsuba's faster divide-and-conquer multiplication.

known.name: Stacks and call stacks
known.gloss: Last-in first-out storage, as used to implement recursive calls with saved return information.

known.name: Pointwise operations on lists and vectors
known.gloss: Applying an operation to corresponding entries of lists or arrays independently, such as pointwise multiplication.

known.name: Sets, subsets and counting
known.gloss: Basic finite set theory and combinatorics: subsets of a given size, intersections, cardinalities and indicator vectors.

known.name: Mathematical induction and proof by contradiction
known.gloss: Standard proof techniques for statements over integers and recursive constructions.

known.name: Euler's formula and complex exponentials
known.gloss: The identity e^{i theta} = cos theta + i sin theta, giving unit-modulus complex numbers and rotations of the complex plane.
